sourcedFrom: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: The Model 700's field strip is one part: the bolt comes out of the receiver and nothing else moves. Remington publishes a genuine deeper procedure past that — barrelled action out of the stock, receiver and trigger assembly flushed and lubricated as a unit, bolt broken down for the firing pin — and the deep branch walks it. The one thing you must settle before you start is which of the three floorplate configurations you own, because it changes what falls out when the stock comes off.

steps.title: Safety fully rearward to "S" before anything else moves
steps.action: Pull the safety mechanism fully to the rear, into the "S" position, and keep your finger off the trigger and outside the guard while you move it.
steps.prose: The 700's safety is a two-position thumb lever on the right of the tang, and this book's version does not lock the bolt handle down — you can lift the bolt and unload with the safety still on "S", which is exactly how it should be done. Get in the habit of moving it with the thumb pad, not the tip of the finger, because a lever that stops halfway between "S" and "F" is neither on nor off. Remington's own instruction is that the safety goes to "S" before handling, loading or unloading, so it goes on before the rifle leaves the rack, not after you have already opened the action.
steps.quote: To engage the safety mechanism, pull the safety mechanism fully to the rear towards the "S" position. See Picture 3.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — Important Parts of the Firearm — The Safety Mechanism, p.7
steps.warn: Remington: the firearm will discharge when the trigger is pulled and the safety mechanism is in the "F" position, and even in "S" careless handling can cause it to discharge.

steps.title: Settle which of the three 700 configurations is in your hands
steps.action: Look at the underside of the stock ahead of the trigger guard and decide which of the three the manual describes you have: a hinged FLOOR PLATE, no floor plate at all (a blind magazine), or a DETACHABLE MAGAZINE BOX.
steps.prose: This is not cosmetic and it is not something the model name settles — a 700 badged ADL is normally the blind-magazine gun, a BDL the hinged-floorplate gun, and an SPS can be built either way or with a detachable box, so the rifle in front of you is the only authority. It decides how you unload: a floorplate rifle dumps its cartridges out of the bottom in one movement, a detachable-box rifle drops its magazine, and a blind-magazine rifle has to have every round cycled out through the ejection port with the bolt. It also decides what happens later in the deep clean — on a rifle without a floor plate the magazine spring and follower are loose in the receiver the moment the stock lifts away, and they will fall on the bench if you are not expecting them.
steps.caution: Remington's book states the three types and does not tell you which you own. Nothing in this guide can resolve it either — read it off the rifle before you go further.
steps.quote: There are three types of Model 700 rifles: (1) with a FLOOR PLATE, (2) without a FLOOR PLATE and (3) with a DETACHABLE MAGAZINE BOX.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — To Load the Firearm, opening line, p.9

steps.title: Bolt back, magazine and chamber empty, then look down the bore
steps.action: Raise the bolt handle, draw the bolt fully to the rear, remove every cartridge from the chamber and the magazine, take the bolt out, and inspect the barrel from the chamber end.
steps.prose: On a bolt gun the chamber and the magazine are two separate places to be wrong about, and a blind-magazine 700 will hold a round under the follower that the ejection port does not show you at a glance — cycle the bolt until nothing more lifts. With the bolt out you are looking straight down a clean, unobstructed tube from the breech, which is also the direction you will clean it in. Remington's book is explicit that an object in the bore is never cleared by firing another cartridge; a rod from the chamber end is the only method it publishes.
steps.quote: l. TO CHECK THE INSIDE OF THE BARREL: 1. Always point the firearm in a safe direction. 2. Place the safety mechanism in the "S" position. 3. Raise the bolt handle. 4. Pull the bolt all the way back. 5. Remove any ammunition from the chamber or magazine. See page 12. 6. Remove the bolt. 7. Inspect the barrel from the chambered end. See Picture 1 on page 7.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — The Barrel — I. To check the inside of the barrel, p.9
steps.warn: Remington: NEVER try to remove an object from the barrel by loading another cartridge and firing. This may cause the barrel to burst or a cartridge case to rupture.

steps.title: Bolt handle up, bolt back, press the bolt stop release inside the guard
steps.action: With the safety still at "S", raise the bolt handle, pull the bolt fully rearward until it stops, then press the bolt stop release inside the front of the trigger guard and slide the bolt assembly out of the receiver.
steps.prose: The bolt stop is a small sprung blade at the left front of the trigger guard opening, not a button on the outside of the receiver — reach a fingertip in from underneath and push it, and the bolt that would not come past that point slides straight out. The feel to expect is a definite stop first, then no resistance at all once the stop is depressed; if the bolt still snags, the stop is not fully down or the handle has not been raised to its full ninety degrees. Support the bolt as it leaves — it is heavy for its size and the extractor claw on the bolt face chips if it lands on concrete.
steps.aside: This same bolt-out state is what every other procedure in the book starts from — barrel cleaning, the stock-off strip and the bolt disassembly all say "remove the bolt assembly" first.
steps.quote: 4. Raise the bolt handle. 5. Pull the bolt handle all the way back. 6. Push the bolt stop release in the trigger guard. See Picture 8. 7. Slide the bolt assembly from the firearm.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — To Remove The Bolt Assembly, steps 4-7, p.8

steps.title: Rifle on its side, port down, and always from the chamber end
steps.action: Lay the barrelled action horizontally with the ejection port facing DOWN, and run every brush and patch from the chamber end out through the muzzle.
steps.prose: Port-down is the whole point: solvent and loosened fouling run out of the open port and onto the bench instead of down into the trigger assembly, which on a 700 sits directly under the loading port and is the one part of the rifle you cannot flush out afterwards without taking the stock off. Cleaning from the chamber end protects the crown, which is what a bolt rifle's accuracy actually lives on — a rod dragged in from the muzzle bears on that edge every stroke. Do not let the rod flex against the chamber mouth either; a bore guide is worth more on a 700 than any solvent you choose.
steps.caution: Remington bars congealing lubricants outright and recommends non-congealing ones; a heavy grease in a 700's bolt raceways stiffens in cold weather and slows lock time.
steps.quote: NOTE: Barrel should lay horizontally with the ejection port facing down during cleaning. Always clean the barrel from the chamber end to the muzzle.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — To Clean the Barrel — note between steps 4 and 5, p.13

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Bolt assembly out, chamber and magazine empty, safety at "S". That is the entire field strip Remington publishes for the Model 700 — the stock, the trigger assembly and the barrelled action all stay together.
steps.prose: With the bolt out you can reach everything the routine clean asks for: the bore from the chamber end, the chamber and locking lug recesses, the bolt face and extractor, and the raceways in the receiver. Anything further — stock screws out, receiver and trigger flushed with action cleaner, firing pin out of the bolt — is the deeper procedure the book prints on pages 13 to 16, and it carries its own safety checks that must pass before the rifle is used again.
steps.quote: For safe and dependable operation of your firearm, the barrel and action must be cleaned periodically.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — Lubrication, p.13

deepSteps.title: Rifle inverted, stock screws out, stock off the barrelled action
deepSteps.action: With the bolt already removed, turn the rifle upside down, back out the stock (trigger guard) screws, and lift the stock away from the receiver and trigger assembly.
deepSteps.prose: There are two screws on a 700 — one ahead of the magazine, one behind it — and on a BDL they pass through the hinged floorplate's trigger guard assembly, which comes away with them. Back both off a turn or two each in alternation rather than running one out fully first, so the action is never levered against a single fastener. Keep them separate and keep them the right way round: the front screw is usually the longer of the two, and swapping them can bottom a screw against the barrel shank or leave the rear one short of thread.
deepSteps.quote: 3. Remove the bolt assembly. See instructions on page 9. 4. Turn the rifle upside down. 5. Remove the stock screws. See Picture 16. 6. Lift the stock away from the receiver and the trigger assembly.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — To Clean the Receiver and The Trigger Assembly, steps 3-6, p.13
deepSteps.warn: The Model Seven and 673 use a different screw pattern from the 700 — the book prints them as separate panels in Picture 16. Work to the picture that matches your rifle.

deepSteps.title: No floor plate? The magazine spring and follower are now loose
deepSteps.action: If yours is the configuration without a floor plate, lift the magazine spring and follower out of the receiver as the stock comes away, and set them aside as a pair.
deepSteps.prose: This is the step that catches people who did not settle the configuration at the start — on a blind-magazine 700 nothing retains the spring and follower except the stock you have just removed, so they can spring out onto the floor the moment it lifts. Note which way up the follower sits before it moves; put back upside down it will not present a cartridge to the bolt face and the rifle will feed the top round nose-first into the barrel shank. A floorplate or detachable-box rifle skips this entirely: its magazine is a captive box that stays where it is.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the magazine spring and follower from the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — To Clean the Receiver and The Trigger Assembly — MODELS WITHOUT A FLOOR PLATE ONLY, p.14

deepSteps.title: The trigger assembly stays bolted to the receiver — clean them as one
deepSteps.action: Do not take the trigger assembly off the receiver. Clean and lubricate the two together, in place, exactly as they sit.
deepSteps.prose: The 700 trigger hangs on two cross pins and its sear engagement is set at the factory; pulling it off is how the engagement, the overtravel and the connector relationship get disturbed, and none of them can be reset by eye. The published method is deliberately a flush-and-cycle rather than a disassembly — solvent in, worked through by operating the parts, blown dry, then oil at four named points. Treat the whole trigger housing as a sealed unit with four holes in it and you will do it right.
deepSteps.quote: Do not remove the trigger assembly from the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — To Clean the Receiver and The Trigger Assembly — note under MODELS WITHOUT A FLOOR PLATE ONLY, p.14
deepSteps.warn: Remington's book allows the owner to adjust the trigger PULL FORCE and nothing else: only the trigger pull force is adjustable, and no other part of the trigger assembly or rifle may be adjusted or altered.

deepSteps.title: Flush the receiver, then the trigger at its four points
deepSteps.action: Spray the receiver thoroughly inside and out with action cleaner and let it dry, then spray inside the trigger assembly at the four points the manual's Picture 17 marks.
deepSteps.prose: Action cleaner is a fast-flashing solvent, not an oil — it is meant to run through the trigger housing carrying grit out with it and then evaporate completely, which is why the book has you dry it before anything else. Do the receiver first and the trigger second so you are not washing receiver debris down into a housing you have just cleaned. Hold the rifle so the trigger housing drains downward and keep spraying until what runs out is clear.
deepSteps.caution: Do not substitute a penetrating oil or a heavy solvent here. Remington warns that a non-recommended lubricant or cleaner can adversely affect the function and safe operation of the firearm.
deepSteps.quote: 7. Thoroughly spray the receiver inside and out with Action Cleaner and allow to dry. 8. Thoroughly spray inside the trigger assembly at the four points specified in Picture 17 with Action Cleaner.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — To Clean the Receiver and The Trigger Assembly, steps 7-8, p.14

deepSteps.title: Work the trigger and prove it returns — every time
deepSteps.action: With the safety at "F", pull the trigger rearward and release it repeatedly, then re-spray, dry, and place one drop of oil at each of the four points. Watch that the trigger comes fully forward on its own after every single release.
deepSteps.prose: This is the part of the deep clean that is a safety test, not a cleaning task: a trigger that hangs back a fraction after release means something in the housing is still gummed or damaged, and the next round can fire when the bolt closes rather than when you ask it to. Do it slowly enough to see the trigger reach its forward stop, not just move. If it ever falls short, Remington's instruction is to reassemble the rifle and send it — not to spray it again and hope.
deepSteps.quote: WARNING! If the trigger does not fully return to the forward position each time it is released, then your rifle is NOT in a safe operating condition and it must NOT be used until you have had it inspected by a Remington Authorized Service Center.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — To Clean the Receiver and The Trigger Assembly — warning after step 14, p.14
deepSteps.warn: A rifle that fails this check does not get fired to "see if it does it again". It goes to a Remington Authorized Service Center.

deepSteps.title: Depress the sear with a punch and watch it snap back up
deepSteps.action: Pull and hold the trigger rearward, press the sear down with a small punch or screwdriver, release it, and repeat several times. The sear must return to the full upward position without hesitation.
deepSteps.prose: The sear is lubrication point 1 in the manual's Picture 17, and it is the surface the cocking piece actually rests on — a sluggish return there is the classic symptom of old oil turned to varnish in a 700 trigger housing. Press it straight down with a punch that fits, not sideways with a screwdriver blade that can nick the engagement face. What you are looking for is a crisp snap back to the top with no lag and no stickiness at any point in the travel.
deepSteps.quote: WARNING! If the sear does not return to the full upward position without hesitation, then your rifle is NOT in a safe operating condition and it must NOT be used until you have had it inspected by a Remington Authorized Service Center.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — To Clean the Receiver and The Trigger Assembly — warning after step 15, p.14

deepSteps.title: Coin in the firing pin head slot, bolt plug counter-clockwise
deepSteps.action: Rest the notch on the firing pin head against a metal edge, pull the bolt body away from the firing pin to compress the mainspring, drop a coin into the slot at the back edge of the firing pin head to hold it there, then turn the bolt plug counter-clockwise until the firing pin assembly lifts out.
deepSteps.prose: The coin is doing the job of a mainspring compressor — it wedges in the slot and holds the cocking piece back off its bearing so the bolt plug unthreads with no spring load fighting it. Do not try this by hand strength alone: the 700 mainspring is stiff and letting the assembly go under load will fire the firing pin head into your palm. Keep the bolt body pointed away from your face throughout, and take the plug off slowly once it comes free of the last thread.
deepSteps.quote: 3. Place the notch on the firing pin head over a metal edge. Pull the bolt assembly away from the firing pin. Place a coin into the slot near the back edge of the firing pin head. See Picture 18.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — Instructions for Cleaning the Bolt Assembly — To Disassemble the Bolt Assembly, step 3, p.16
deepSteps.warn: Remington: clean the firing pin assembly AS A UNIT. It is not broken down further by the owner.

deepSteps.title: Re-cock the bolt on reassembly, or it will not go back in the rifle
deepSteps.action: Put the firing pin assembly into the rear of the bolt, hand-tighten the bolt plug, pull the coin out of the slot, then turn the bolt plug until the firing pin head drops into the small notch on the rear rim of the bolt. That is the cocked position.
deepSteps.prose: A 700 bolt will only enter the receiver cocked, because uncocked the cocking piece stands proud at the back and fouls the bridge. You feel the cocked position rather than see it — the head settles down into the small notch with a distinct click and the bolt plug stops turning easily. If the bolt refuses to go into the rifle, do not force it; take it back out and check that notch, because that is the fault nine times out of ten.
deepSteps.aside: The book says it plainly a line later: the bolt must be cocked to be assembled into the rifle.
deepSteps.quote: 5. Turn the bolt plug until the firing pin head goes into the small notch on the rear rim of the bolt. The bolt is now cocked. See Picture 19.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — Instructions for Cleaning the Bolt Assembly — To Assemble, step 5, p.16

cleaning.name: BORE, CHAMBER & CROWN
tasks: Lay the barrelled action horizontally with the ejection port facing DOWN so solvent drains away from the trigger, not into it
Correct-calibre brush wet with solvent, chamber end to muzzle, several passes — never reverse a brush inside the bore
Swap to a jag and patch and repeat with a fresh patch each time until one comes out clean
Oiled patch through, then a dry patch behind it — a 700 left with oil in the chamber will let the case slip and batter the bolt face
Wipe the outside of the barrel with a lightly oiled cloth; stainless synthetic 700s are corrosion RESISTANT, not corrosion proof

cleaning.name: BOLT, LUGS & EXTRACTOR
tasks: Solvent and a brush across the bolt face, into the extractor cut and around the plunger ejector
Work the ejector plunger in and out — a 700 ejector that sticks down leaves the case sitting on the bolt face
Clean the two locking lugs and their bearing surfaces, then the locking lug recesses in the receiver ring
Dry everything, then a thin film of non-congealing oil on the lugs and the bolt body — never a congealing grease
Clean the firing pin assembly as a unit only; it is not disassembled further

cleaning.name: RECEIVER & TRIGGER (deep only)
tasks: Receiver sprayed inside and out with action cleaner and allowed to dry
Trigger assembly flushed at the four points of Picture 17, cycled with trigger and sear, flushed again, blown dry
One drop of oil at each of the four points — one drop, not a spray
Trigger-return and sear-return checks both passed before the rifle is put back together
Light oil on the external surfaces of trigger assembly and receiver, excess wiped off

reassembly: Blind-magazine rifles first: magazine follower and spring back into the magazine the right way up, follower cartridge face upward.
Stock over the receiver and trigger assembly; on a floorplate or detachable-box rifle assemble the trigger guard onto the stock first.
Replace and tighten both stock (trigger guard) screws, drawing them down alternately rather than one at a time.
Close the floor plate, or seat the detachable magazine.
Check the barrel is free of obstructions BEFORE the bolt goes back — Remington puts that warning immediately ahead of this step.
Bolt cocked, lugs aligned with the receiver cuts, slide it fully in and drop the handle.
Dry-patch the bore and chamber before the rifle is fired or stored.
fncheck: With the chamber and magazine confirmed empty: put the safety at "F", close the bolt smartly, and confirm the firing pin stays cocked — then pull the trigger and confirm it releases. Remington's instruction is to repeat that test at least ten times; a firing pin that will not stay cocked when the bolt is closed smartly means the rifle goes to the factory or a Remington Authorized Service Center. Also confirm the trigger returns fully forward after every release, that the sear snaps back to the top without hesitation, and that the safety goes fully to "S" and fully to "F" without stopping anywhere in between.
